# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## funes
Persistent memory over the user's past AI coding sessions: their transcripts, indexed automatically as they work and read-only here — nothing has to be saved. When earlier work matters, this is the memory to consult.

The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- devboxes: Creates, runs, shares, and tears down Namespace devboxes with `devbox` or `boxctl`. Use for isolated Linux or macOS environments, remote builds or tests, disposable Docker hosts, workloads exceeding local capacity, exposing `devbox.so` URLs, or working inside a devbox (`NAMESPACE_DEVBOX_WORKSPACE_DIR` is set), including keeping unattended work alive with task markers.
- ripwire-before-you-build: Starting a FEATURE (multi-symbol work): the plan, the API boundary, the scope — how big does this change get — from the codebase's real structure. Implementing an EXISTING interface? --lego=Iface lists its contract and current implementors. ONE standalone symbol → reuse-first. A small feature with an obvious home needs none of this.
- ripwire-change-check: Merge-SAFETY of an existing diff — yours before you push, or a PR you review: blast radius, tests to run, a broken contract (--edit-check=SYM), branch conflicts and landing order, unmerged work stranded on old branches, which ref defines it. Code QUALITY → quality-bar. Even a one-line leaf fix runs --edit-check.
- ripwire-find-bug: You have a SYMPTOM — crash, exception, wrong output, failing test, error string — and don't know which code is responsible. Ranks candidates; a stack trace or sanitizer output maps onto frames innermost-first; 'it worked yesterday' / 'my last edit broke it' → --situ. One clear hit plus one focused read is enough.
- ripwire-fresh-eyes: Maintenance risk in code you did NOT write — inheriting a module, planning a refactor, a suspected god object, 'what's gnarly / where's the rot / safe to touch?': hotspots, dead or inactive code, switches/defaults (--flags), clones, a function's real shape, bus factor, co-change. Naming the fix or judging YOUR new code → quality-bar. A single-lens question is a single call.
- ripwire-graph-query: A call-graph question the fixed verbs can't phrase — 'which high-complexity functions can reach X?', 'what has 10+ callers in src/?', 'untested symbols within one hop of main'. --graph-query: a small closed expression language — kind, complexity, fan-in, tested filters; a file or cluster; bounded hops; and/or/not.
- ripwire-handoff: Brief someone ELSE on a subsystem — 'hand this area off' to a successor, teammate or fresh session: purpose, the 2-3 entry points with bodies, the design docs that say WHY, hotspot/bus-factor risk — a compact pasteable brief, not a wall of source. Understanding it yourself → orient.
- ripwire-layers: Architecture HEALTH and ENFORCEMENT — 'is this a dependency mess / does the UI reach into the database / enforce module boundaries in CI?': cycles, the godfile, propagation cost (how far a touch ripples), --arch rules with a baseline gate. Overview without gating → orient. One pass answers it.
- ripwire-mcp: Wire ripwire into an agent as an MCP server — `ripwire wrap AGENT` (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini…) — and choose the server verb mid-task. Also tool HEALTH: a symbol you expected is missing from the ranked output, the index feels stale after a rebase, 'is my ripwire setup broken?'
- ripwire-navigate: You can NAME the symbol: who calls it, what it calls, the path from A to B, its full body, or an exact literal/regex match. 'Safe to change or rename X — what breaks downstream?' = the transitive blast radius, not 1-hop callers. Three or more symbols → --connect. Run the one verb that fits, then stop.
- ripwire-orient: Landing COLD in an unfamiliar repo or subsystem, or about to open several files for one question: map first, read only what it ranks highest — main subsystems, entry points, 'how does X work / where is Y'. Also recover context after compaction, retrieve saved docs (--recall), divide code for subagents (--partition), save gotchas (--note-add). NAMED symbol → navigate. Stop at the first rung that answers.
- ripwire-perf-target: A MEASURED performance problem: start from a benchmark, flame graph, perf sample or profiler run, locate the hot symbol the profile names, test structural hypotheses (memory-bound → cache-line data layout). Static metrics are change-risk signals, not runtime heat. Inspect only the symbols the profile names.
- ripwire-quality-bar: Code QUALITY of what YOU just wrote, before you commit or say 'done', or verifying a cleanup: --quality-delta lists what got WORSE in 10 kinds and exits 2 only when pre-existing code got materially worse; which restructuring a measured shape (humps/deep, a tangle) calls for. Merge safety → change-check. Even a single-line leaf fix runs it.
- ripwire-reuse-first: About to write ONE symbol (even a 'quick' one-liner) or add a dependency: reuse before you reinvent. Finds the building block that already exists, the house pattern to imitate, the duplicate you'd recreate, a vendored dependency. An interface or whole feature → before-you-build. One --exemplar or --grep call at most.
- ripwire-router: Start HERE when unsure which ripwire skill fits, or asked 'how do I use ripwire / where do I start'. A moment→skill map, cold start to handoff, plus the two reflexes that leak most: --exemplar before you write, --quality-delta before you call it done. One hop to the right skill.
- ripwire-security-scan: Security review: (1) vet an untrusted SKILL.md or .mcp.json BEFORE installing it — the injection/exfiltration scanner; CRITICAL blocks the install; (2) audit code on an untrusted-input path (a deserializer, parser, exec of user data, network endpoint): taint reach, untested seams. One scan pass is the verdict.
- ripwire-write-tests: Write tests for EXISTING code that has none — 'this is untested, add coverage', 'add a safety net first'; also verify a new test reaches its intended code. Finds what no test reaches: --seams ranks untested cross-module edges, --callers gives the outside contract. Diff test selection → change-check. For one target one --seams or --callers pass suffices.
- typesafe-ai: Build AI-powered software with TypeSafe: small units of AI intelligence you can use like programming primitives. Its System One models, including Jev, turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision. Applications include routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive experiences; these are starting points, not the limits. Read live docs and cookbooks to find useful patterns and discover new combinations.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- funes:funes: Persistent memory over the user's past AI coding sessions, searched and read through the funes MCP tools. Use when the user refers to earlier work, asks what memory is available, or when a past session may already have settled the question.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.TaxDeductionClaim
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.User
  alias ZaimuTomo.Currency
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Fingerprint
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision

  @need_or_want_values ["need", "want"]
  @duplicate_invoice_index "journal_entries_user_issuer_number_unique_index"
  @duplicate_source_file_index "journal_entries_user_source_document_sha256_unique_index"

  @typedoc "Journal entry schema struct"
  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          __meta__: Ecto.Schema.Metadata.t(),
          id: integer() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          currency: String.t() | nil,
          date: Date.t() | nil,
          description: String.t() | nil,
          issuer: String.t() | nil,
          invoice_number: String.t() | nil,
          category: String.t() | nil,
          need_or_want: String.t() | nil,
          status: String.t() | nil,
          notes: String.t() | nil,
          source_document_sha256: String.t() | nil,
          source_file_reuse_confirmed: boolean(),
          review_decision_id: integer() | nil,
          user_id: integer() | nil,
          review_decision: Ecto.Schema.belongs_to(struct()),
          user: Ecto.Schema.belongs_to(struct()),
          tax_deduction_claim: Ecto.Schema.has_one(TaxDeductionClaim.t()),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  schema "journal_entries" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :currency, :string
    field :date, :date
    field :description, :string
    field :issuer, :string
    field :invoice_number, :string
    field :category, :string
    field :need_or_want, :string
    field :status, :string
    field :notes, :string
    # Posting-time snapshot of the source document's fingerprint. Only the
    # one-off backfill may set it on an existing row (see the backfill module).
    field :source_document_sha256, :string, redact: true
    field :source_file_reuse_confirmed, :boolean, default: false

    belongs_to :review_decision, ReviewDecision
    belongs_to :user, User
    has_one :tax_deduction_claim, TaxDeductionClaim

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @spec changeset_for_create(map()) :: Ecto.Changeset.t(t())
  def changeset_for_create(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :review_decision_id,
      :user_id,
      :amount_cents,
      :currency,
      :date,
      :description,
      :issuer,
      :invoice_number,
      :status,
      :source_document_sha256,
      :source_file_reuse_confirmed
    ])
    |> Currency.normalize_and_validate(:currency)
    |> validate_required([:review_decision_id, :user_id, :amount_cents, :currency, :date])
    |> validate_inclusion(:status, ["uncategorized", "posted"])
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:review_decision_id)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:user_id)
    |> unique_constraint(:review_decision_id)
    |> fingerprint_constraints()
    |> unique_constraint(:invoice_number,
      name: @duplicate_invoice_index,
      message: "has already been recorded for this issuer"
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the historical fingerprint backfill: the only permitted update
  of `source_document_sha256` (and, for a human-resolved collision,
  `source_file_reuse_confirmed`) on an existing entry.
  """
  @spec changeset_for_fingerprint_backfill(t(), map()) :: Ecto.Changeset.t(t())
  def changeset_for_fingerprint_backfill(%__MODULE__{} = entry, attrs) do
    entry
    |> cast(attrs, [:source_document_sha256, :source_file_reuse_confirmed])
    |> validate_required([:source_document_sha256])
    |> fingerprint_constraints()
  end

  defp fingerprint_constraints(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:source_document_sha256, Fingerprint.format())
    |> unique_constraint(:source_document_sha256,
      name: @duplicate_source_file_index,
      message: "the same file has already been recorded"
    )
  end

  @doc "Name of the unique (user, issuer, invoice number) index."
  @spec duplicate_invoice_index() :: String.t()
  def duplicate_invoice_index, do: @duplicate_invoice_index

  @doc "Name of the unique (user, source file digest) index over unconfirmed postings."
  @spec duplicate_source_file_index() :: String.t()
  def duplicate_source_file_index, do: @duplicate_source_file_index

  @spec changeset_for_categorize(t(), map()) :: Ecto.Changeset.t(t())
  def changeset_for_categorize(%__MODULE__{} = entry, attrs) do
    entry
    |> cast(attrs, [:category, :need_or_want, :notes, :status])
    |> validate_required([:category, :need_or_want])
    |> validate_inclusion(:need_or_want, @need_or_want_values)
    |> validate_inclusion(:status, ["uncategorized", "posted"])
    |> check_constraint(:need_or_want, name: :journal_entries_need_or_want_check)
  end

  @spec need_or_want_values() :: [String.t()]
  def need_or_want_values, do: @need_or_want_values
end
      TaxDeductionClaim.changeset_for_create(entry, tax_claim_attrs) |> repo.insert()
    end)
    |> maybe_post_booking(Keyword.get(opts, :booking))
  end

  defp maybe_post_booking(multi, nil), do: multi

  defp maybe_post_booking(multi, booking) when is_map(booking) do
    Multi.update(multi, :posted_journal_entry, fn %{journal_entry: entry} ->
      booking = Map.new(booking, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

      JournalEntry.changeset_for_categorize(entry, Map.put(booking, "status", "posted"))
    end)
  end

  @doc """

  (user, issuer, invoice number) index or the unique (user, source file

Uploads record a SHA-256 of their exact bytes (`documents.content_sha256`), and
postings copy it to `journal_entries.source_document_sha256`. Rows created
before the `20261017120000` migration have no fingerprint until this one-off
backfill reads their objects. The unique index exists before it runs, so it is
safe while the app stays online; no upload or approval pause is needed.

1. Run `kamal backfill_document_fingerprints`. It hashes every document with a
   null digest through the storage facade, then copies digests to journal
   entries one row at a time, oldest posting first. The report lists IDs and
   counts only, never bytes or digests. It exits non-zero while coverage is
   incomplete.
2. Read the report:
   - **Missing object / read failure:** the digest stays null; that document and
     its entries have no exact-file protection. Restore the object if a backup
     has it (then rerun), otherwise record the partial coverage.
   - **Collision:** two historical postings of the same user have identical
     bytes. The later entry stays null and is named with the entry it collides
     with. Nothing is deleted or merged. Review both entries in the ledger:
     a genuine duplicate is corrected through the normal ledger process; a
     legitimate reuse (for example, the same QR-bill for two periods) is
     confirmed by a human.
3. To record a human-confirmed reuse, rerun with the later entry's ID:
   `kamal app exec "bin/backfill_document_fingerprints <journal_entry_id> ..."`
   (locally, `mix zaimu_tomo.backfill_document_fingerprints --confirm-reuse <id>`).
   The entry gets its digest and `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. An
   ID that does not collide is reported as unused and left unchanged.
4. Rerun after any resolution until it reports complete coverage, or until the
   only remaining rows are documented missing objects.

This is the only permitted update of an existing entry's fingerprint. If a

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Release do
  @moduledoc """
  Release helpers used by deployment tasks.
  """

  @app :zaimu_tomo

  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage.{Migration, Verification}

  def migrate do
    load_app()

    for repo <- repos() do
      {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :up, all: true))
    end
  end

  def rollback(repo, version) do
    load_app()
    {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :down, to: version))
  end

  def migrate_to_s3!(source_dir) when is_binary(source_dir) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Migration.migrate(source_dir), Migration)
  end

  def migrate_to_s3_from_env! do
    System.fetch_env!("SOURCE_DIR")
    |> migrate_to_s3!()
  end

  def backfill_document_fingerprints!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(FingerprintBackfill.run(opts), FingerprintBackfill)
  end

  def verify_storage! do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Verification.verify(), Verification)
  end

  def recover_stuck_documents!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    groups = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.list_stuck()
    Enum.each(groups, &print_stuck_group/1)

    dispatch_recovery(Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false), groups)
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(true, groups) do
    jobs = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.enqueue_stuck(groups)
    IO.puts("Enqueued #{length(jobs)} OCR jobs.")
    groups
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(false, groups) do
    count = groups |> Enum.map(&length(&1.document_ids)) |> Enum.sum()
    IO.puts("Dry run: #{count} stuck documents — nothing enqueued.")
    IO.puts("Re-run with confirm: true (or CONFIRM=true) to enqueue.")
    groups
  end

  defp print_stuck_group(%{user_id: user_id, currency: currency, document_ids: document_ids}) do
    IO.puts("user #{user_id} (#{currency}): document ids #{Enum.join(document_ids, ", ")}")
  end

  defp repos do
    Application.fetch_env!(@app, :ecto_repos)
  end

  defp load_app do
    Application.load(@app)
  end

  defp start_app do
    load_app()

    # Eval nodes run maintenance only: no queues, no plugins, no leadership, so
    # a short-lived node never grabs a job and dies mid-run (leaving it orphaned
    # until Lifeline rescues it).
    oban = Application.fetch_env!(@app, Oban)

    Application.put_env(
      @app,
      Oban,
      Keyword.merge(oban, queues: false, plugins: false, peer: false)
    )

    case Application.ensure_all_started(@app) do
      {:ok, _started} -> :ok
      {:error, reason} -> raise "could not start #{@app}: #{inspect(reason)}"
    end
  end

  defp report_or_raise({status, summary}, formatter) do
    IO.puts(formatter.format_summary(summary))

    case status do
      :ok -> summary
      :error -> raise "storage maintenance command failed"
    end
  end
end
defmodule ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill do
  @moduledoc """
  Idempotent, online backfill of exact-byte fingerprints for rows created
  before fingerprints existed.

  1. Every document with a null `content_sha256` is read through
     `ZaimuTomo.Storage` and hashed. A missing or unreadable object is
     reported and left null; no other value is ever stored in its place.
  2. Every journal entry with a null `source_document_sha256` receives its
     source document's fingerprint, one entry per update and oldest first, so
     the first posting of a file keeps it. A unique-index violation (a same-user
     historical duplicate) affects only that row: it is reported with the entry
     it collides with and left null. Ledger rows are never deleted or merged.

  A human may resolve a reported collision by listing the later entry in
  `:confirm_reuse`; the backfill then sets its digest and
  `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. This is the only permitted
  update of an existing entry's fingerprint (spec D7), so it must run before
  any database-level immutability trigger on `journal_entries` exists, or that
  trigger must allow it.

  The report contains row IDs and counts only, never bytes or digests. The
  partial unique index already exists, so concurrent postings cannot create a
  same-user duplicate while this runs.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Fingerprint
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage

  @type collision :: %{journal_entry_id: integer(), user_id: integer(), conflicts_with: integer()}

  @type summary :: %{
          documents_hashed: non_neg_integer(),
          documents_already_complete: non_neg_integer(),
          missing_objects: [integer()],
          read_failures: [%{document_id: integer(), reason: term()}],
          entries_updated: non_neg_integer(),
          entries_already_complete: non_neg_integer(),
          entries_reuse_confirmed: [integer()],
          entries_source_unavailable: [integer()],
          collisions: [collision()],
          unused_reuse_confirmations: [integer()]
        }

  @doc """
  Runs the backfill.

  Returns `{:ok, summary}` when historical coverage is complete, and
  `{:error, summary}` when any object is missing or unreadable, an entry's
  source fingerprint is unavailable, or a collision awaits human review.

  Options:

    * `:confirm_reuse` — journal entry IDs a human confirmed as legitimate
      reuses of an already posted file. Applied only to an entry whose plain
      update collides; otherwise reported as unused.
  """
  @spec run(keyword()) :: {:ok, summary()} | {:error, summary()}
  def run(opts \\ []) do
    confirm_reuse = opts |> Keyword.get(:confirm_reuse, []) |> MapSet.new()

    summary =
      empty_summary()
      |> backfill_documents()
      |> backfill_journal_entries(confirm_reuse)
      |> finalize(confirm_reuse)

    if complete?(summary), do: {:ok, summary}, else: {:error, summary}
  end

  @spec format_summary(summary()) :: String.t()
  def format_summary(summary) do
    [
      "Fingerprint backfill summary: " <>
        "documents_hashed=#{summary.documents_hashed} " <>
        "documents_already_complete=#{summary.documents_already_complete} " <>
        "missing_objects=#{length(summary.missing_objects)} " <>
        "read_failures=#{length(summary.read_failures)} " <>
        "entries_updated=#{summary.entries_updated} " <>
        "entries_already_complete=#{summary.entries_already_complete} " <>
        "entries_reuse_confirmed=#{length(summary.entries_reuse_confirmed)} " <>
        "entries_source_unavailable=#{length(summary.entries_source_unavailable)} " <>
        "collisions=#{length(summary.collisions)}"

.rwxrwxr-x   237 alexis  6 Sep 22:31  migrate_to_s3
.rwxrwxr-x   246 alexis 18 Oct 15:15  recover_stuck_documents
.rwxrwxr-x   110 alexis  6 Sep 22:31  verify_storage

  defp row_data(%{extracted_data: data}), do: data
  defp row_data(nil), do: nil

  # "Needs action" is everything the user still has to do something about:
  # an invoice to check, and a failed or stalled extraction to retry.
  defp in_tab?("all", _status), do: true

  defp in_tab?("needs_action", status),
    do: status in ["review", "failed", "stalled", "processing"]

  defp in_tab?("posted", status), do: status == "posted"
  defp in_tab?("rejected", status), do: status == "rejected"

  defp tab_path("all"), do: ~p"/documents"
  defp tab_path(tab), do: ~p"/documents?tab=#{tab}"

postings copy it to `journal_entries.source_document_sha256`. Rows created
before the `20261017120000` migration have no fingerprint until this one-off
backfill reads their objects. The unique index exists before it runs, so it is
safe while the app stays online; no upload or approval pause is needed.

1. Run `kamal backfill_document_fingerprints`. It hashes every document with a
   null digest through the storage facade, then copies digests to journal
   entries one row at a time, oldest posting first. The report lists IDs and
   counts only, never bytes or digests. It exits non-zero while coverage is
   incomplete.
2. Read the report:
   - **Missing object / read failure:** the digest stays null; that document and
     its entries have no exact-file protection. Restore the object if a backup
     has it (then rerun), otherwise record the partial coverage.
   - **Collision:** two historical postings of the same user have identical
     bytes. The later entry stays null and is named with the entry it collides
     with. Nothing is deleted or merged. Review both entries in the ledger:
     a genuine duplicate is corrected through the normal ledger process; a
     legitimate reuse (for example, the same QR-bill for two periods) is
     confirmed by a human.
3. To record a human-confirmed reuse, rerun with the later entry's ID:
   `kamal app exec "bin/backfill_document_fingerprints <journal_entry_id> ..."`
   (locally, `mix zaimu_tomo.backfill_document_fingerprints --confirm-reuse <id>`).
   The entry gets its digest and `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. An
   ID that does not collide is reported as unused and left unchanged.
4. Rerun after any resolution until it reports complete coverage, or until the
   only remaining rows are documented missing objects.

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Release do
  @moduledoc """
  Release helpers used by deployment tasks.
  """

  @app :zaimu_tomo

  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage.{Migration, Verification}

  def migrate do
    load_app()

    for repo <- repos() do
      {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :up, all: true))
    end
  end

  def rollback(repo, version) do
    load_app()
    {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :down, to: version))
  end

  def migrate_to_s3!(source_dir) when is_binary(source_dir) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Migration.migrate(source_dir), Migration)
  end

  def migrate_to_s3_from_env! do
    System.fetch_env!("SOURCE_DIR")
    |> migrate_to_s3!()
  end

  def backfill_document_fingerprints!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(FingerprintBackfill.run(opts), FingerprintBackfill)
  end

  def verify_storage! do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Verification.verify(), Verification)
  end

  def recover_stuck_documents!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    groups = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.list_stuck()
    Enum.each(groups, &print_stuck_group/1)

    dispatch_recovery(Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false), groups)
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(true, groups) do
    jobs = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.enqueue_stuck(groups)
    IO.puts("Enqueued #{length(jobs)} OCR jobs.")
    groups
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(false, groups) do
    count = groups |> Enum.map(&length(&1.document_ids)) |> Enum.sum()
    IO.puts("Dry run: #{count} stuck documents — nothing enqueued.")
    IO.puts("Re-run with confirm: true (or CONFIRM=true) to enqueue.")
    groups
  end

  defp print_stuck_group(%{user_id: user_id, currency: currency, document_ids: document_ids}) do
    IO.puts("user #{user_id} (#{currency}): document ids #{Enum.join(document_ids, ", ")}")
  end

  defp repos do
    Application.fetch_env!(@app, :ecto_repos)
  end

  defp load_app do
    Application.load(@app)
  end

  defp start_app do
    load_app()

    # Eval nodes run maintenance only: no queues, no plugins, no leadership, so
    # a short-lived node never grabs a job and dies mid-run (leaving it orphaned
    # until Lifeline rescues it).
    oban = Application.fetch_env!(@app, Oban)

    Application.put_env(
      @app,
      Oban,
      Keyword.merge(oban, queues: false, plugins: false, peer: false)
    )

    case Application.ensure_all_started(@app) do
      {:ok, _started} -> :ok
      {:error, reason} -> raise "could not start #{@app}: #{inspect(reason)}"
    end
  end

  defp report_or_raise({status, summary}, formatter) do
    IO.puts(formatter.format_summary(summary))

    case status do
      :ok -> summary
      :error -> raise "storage maintenance command failed"
    end
  end
end
defmodule ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill do
  @moduledoc """
  Idempotent, online backfill of exact-byte fingerprints for rows created
  before fingerprints existed.

  1. Every document with a null `content_sha256` is read through
     `ZaimuTomo.Storage` and hashed. A missing or unreadable object is
     reported and left null; no other value is ever stored in its place.
  2. Every journal entry with a null `source_document_sha256` receives its
     source document's fingerprint, one entry per update and oldest first, so
     the first posting of a file keeps it. A unique-index violation (a same-user
     historical duplicate) affects only that row: it is reported with the entry
     it collides with and left null. Ledger rows are never deleted or merged.

  A human may resolve a reported collision by listing the later entry in
  `:confirm_reuse`; the backfill then sets its digest and
  `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. This is the only permitted
  update of an existing entry's fingerprint (spec D7), so it must run before
  any database-level immutability trigger on `journal_entries` exists, or that
  trigger must allow it.

  The report contains row IDs and counts only, never bytes or digests. The
  partial unique index already exists, so concurrent postings cannot create a
  same-user duplicate while this runs.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Fingerprint
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage

  @type collision :: %{journal_entry_id: integer(), user_id: integer(), conflicts_with: integer()}

  @type summary :: %{
          documents_hashed: non_neg_integer(),
          documents_already_complete: non_neg_integer(),
          missing_objects: [integer()],
          read_failures: [%{document_id: integer(), reason: term()}],
          entries_updated: non_neg_integer(),
          entries_already_complete: non_neg_integer(),
          entries_reuse_confirmed: [integer()],
          entries_source_unavailable: [integer()],
          collisions: [collision()],
          unused_reuse_confirmations: [integer()]
        }

  @doc """
  Runs the backfill.

  Returns `{:ok, summary}` when historical coverage is complete, and
  `{:error, summary}` when any object is missing or unreadable, an entry's
  source fingerprint is unavailable, or a collision awaits human review.

  Options:

    * `:confirm_reuse` — journal entry IDs a human confirmed as legitimate
      reuses of an already posted file. Applied only to an entry whose plain
      update collides; otherwise reported as unused.
  """
  @spec run(keyword()) :: {:ok, summary()} | {:error, summary()}
  def run(opts \\ []) do
    confirm_reuse = opts |> Keyword.get(:confirm_reuse, []) |> MapSet.new()

    summary =
      empty_summary()
      |> backfill_documents()
      |> backfill_journal_entries(confirm_reuse)
      |> finalize(confirm_reuse)

    if complete?(summary), do: {:ok, summary}, else: {:error, summary}
  end

  @spec format_summary(summary()) :: String.t()
  def format_summary(summary) do
    [
      "Fingerprint backfill summary: " <>
        "documents_hashed=#{summary.documents_hashed} " <>
        "documents_already_complete=#{summary.documents_already_complete} " <>
        "missing_objects=#{length(summary.missing_objects)} " <>
        "read_failures=#{length(summary.read_failures)} " <>
        "entries_updated=#{summary.entries_updated} " <>
        "entries_already_complete=#{summary.entries_already_complete} " <>
        "entries_reuse_confirmed=#{length(summary.entries_reuse_confirmed)} " <>
        "entries_source_unavailable=#{length(summary.entries_source_unavailable)} " <>
        "collisions=#{length(summary.collisions)}"

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.TaxDeductionClaim do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.User

  @statuses ["undecided", "candidate", "not_deductible", "claimed", "disallowed"]

  @typedoc "Tax deduction claim schema struct"
  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          __meta__: Ecto.Schema.Metadata.t(),
          id: integer() | nil,
          tax_year: integer() | nil,
          status: String.t() | nil,
          category: String.t() | nil,
          deductible_amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          notes: String.t() | nil,
          journal_entry_id: integer() | nil,
          user_id: integer() | nil,
          journal_entry: Ecto.Schema.belongs_to(JournalEntry.t()),
          user: Ecto.Schema.belongs_to(struct()),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  schema "tax_deduction_claims" do
    field :tax_year, :integer
    field :status, :string, default: "undecided"
    field :category, :string
    field :deductible_amount_cents, :integer
    field :notes, :string

    belongs_to :journal_entry, JournalEntry
    belongs_to :user, User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @typep persisted_journal_entry :: %JournalEntry{
           id: integer(),
           amount_cents: integer(),
           date: Date.t(),
           user_id: integer()
         }

  @spec changeset_for_create(persisted_journal_entry(), map()) :: Ecto.Changeset.t(t())
  def changeset_for_create(%JournalEntry{} = entry, attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{
      journal_entry_id: entry.id,
      user_id: entry.user_id,
      tax_year: entry.date.year,
      deductible_amount_cents: entry.amount_cents
    }
    |> cast(attrs, [:status, :category, :deductible_amount_cents, :notes])
    |> validate_required([
      :journal_entry_id,
      :user_id,
      :tax_year,
      :status,
      :deductible_amount_cents
    ])
    |> validate_inclusion(:status, @statuses)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:journal_entry_id)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:user_id)
    |> unique_constraint(:journal_entry_id)
    |> check_constraint(:status, name: :tax_deduction_claims_status_check)
  end

  @spec changeset_for_update(t(), map()) :: Ecto.Changeset.t(t())
  def changeset_for_update(%__MODULE__{} = claim, attrs) do
    claim
    |> cast(attrs, [:status, :category, :deductible_amount_cents, :notes])
    |> validate_required([:status, :deductible_amount_cents])
    |> validate_inclusion(:status, @statuses)
    |> check_constraint(:status, name: :tax_deduction_claims_status_check)
  end

  @spec status_options() :: [{String.t(), String.t()}]
  def status_options do
    [
      {"Not yet decided", "undecided"},
      {"Potentially deductible", "candidate"},
      {"Not deductible", "not_deductible"}
    ]
  end

  @spec status_label(String.t() | nil) :: String.t()
  def status_label("undecided"), do: "Not yet decided"
  def status_label("candidate"), do: "Potentially deductible"
  def status_label("not_deductible"), do: "Not deductible"
  def status_label("claimed"), do: "Included in tax return"
  def status_label("disallowed"), do: "Not allowed"
  def status_label(_), do: "—"
end

  def create_multi_from_decision(
        %ReviewDecision{} = decision,
        tax_claim_attrs \\ %{},
        opts \\ []
      ) do
    data = decision.decision_data || decision.original_data

    attrs = %{
      review_decision_id: decision.id,
      user_id: decision.user_id,
      amount_cents: data.amount_to_pay_cents,
      currency: data.currency,
      date: parse_date(data.invoice_date),
      description: data.reason_for_payment,
      issuer: data.issuer,
      invoice_number: data.invoice_number,
      status: "uncategorized",
      source_document_sha256: Keyword.get(opts, :source_document_sha256),
      source_file_reuse_confirmed: Keyword.get(opts, :source_file_reuse_confirmed, false)
    }

    tax_claim_attrs = normalize_tax_claim_attrs(attrs.amount_cents, tax_claim_attrs)

    Multi.new()
    |> Multi.insert(:journal_entry, JournalEntry.changeset_for_create(attrs))
    |> Multi.run(:tax_deduction_claim, fn repo, %{journal_entry: entry} ->
      TaxDeductionClaim.changeset_for_create(entry, tax_claim_attrs) |> repo.insert()

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfill do
  @moduledoc """
  One-off backfill for journal entries that predate booking at posting time and
  are still missing a category or a need/want choice.

  An entry is completed only when the same user's posted entries from the same
  issuer (compared like the duplicate index, trimmed and case-insensitive) agree
  on every missing value. Values the entry already has are kept. Anything else
  is reported for a person to book, so nothing is guessed from a similar name.

  It is a dry run unless called with `confirm: true`. Each entry is updated in
  its own transaction together with a `journal_entry_booking_backfilled` event
  that records the prior state. Tax claims and notes are left alone, and
  `updated_at` is kept so old entries do not jump to the top of the journal.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias Ecto.Multi
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.EventLog
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision

  @event_type "journal_entry_booking_backfilled"

  @type match :: %{
          entry: JournalEntry.t(),
          document_id: integer(),
          category: String.t(),
          need_or_want: String.t(),
          precedent_count: pos_integer()
        }

  @type unmatched :: %{
          entry: JournalEntry.t(),
          document_id: integer(),
          reason: :no_history | :conflicting_history
        }

  @type summary :: %{
          confirmed: boolean(),
          matched: [match()],
          applied: [match()],
          unmatched: [unmatched()],
          failed: [%{match: match(), errors: term()}]
        }

  @doc """
  Plans the backfill and, with `confirm: true`, applies it.

  Returns `{:error, summary}` only when an update failed. Unmatched entries are
  expected and left for manual booking.
  """
  @spec run(keyword()) :: {:ok, summary()} | {:error, summary()}
  def run(opts \\ []) do
    confirmed = Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false)
    %{matched: matched, unmatched: unmatched} = plan()
    %{applied: applied, failed: failed} = apply_matches(matched, confirmed)

    summary = %{
      confirmed: confirmed,
      matched: matched,
      applied: applied,
      unmatched: unmatched,
      failed: failed
    }

    {if(failed == [], do: :ok, else: :error), summary}
  end

  @spec format_summary(summary()) :: String.t()
  def format_summary(summary) do
    verb = if summary.confirmed, do: "Booked", else: "Would book"
    mode = if summary.confirmed, do: "applied", else: "dry run"

    [
      "Legacy booking backfill (#{mode}): matched=#{length(summary.matched)} " <>
        "applied=#{length(summary.applied)} unmatched=#{length(summary.unmatched)} " <>
        "failed=#{length(summary.failed)}",
      Enum.map(summary.matched, &format_match(&1, verb)),
      Enum.map(summary.unmatched, &format_unmatched/1),
      Enum.map(summary.failed, &format_failure/1),
      if(summary.confirmed, do: [], else: "Nothing changed. Re-run with confirm: true to apply.")
    ]
    |> List.flatten()
    |> Enum.join("\n")
  end

  defp plan do
    precedents = precedents()

    targets()
    |> Enum.map(&classify(&1, precedents))
    |> Enum.group_by(&elem(&1, 0), &elem(&1, 1))
    |> then(&%{matched: Map.get(&1, :matched, []), unmatched: Map.get(&1, :unmatched, [])})
  end

  defp targets do
    Repo.all(
      from e in JournalEntry,
        join: d in ReviewDecision,
        on: d.id == e.review_decision_id,
        join: c in ExtractedContent,
        on: c.id == d.extracted_content_id,
        where: is_nil(e.category) or is_nil(e.need_or_want),
        order_by: e.id,
        select: %{
          entry: e,
          document_id: c.document_id,
          issuer_key: fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer)
        }
    )
  end

  defp precedents do
    from(e in JournalEntry,
      where: e.status == "posted",
      where: not is_nil(e.category) and not is_nil(e.need_or_want),
      where: fragment("btrim(?) <> ''", e.issuer),
      group_by: [e.user_id, fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer), e.category, e.need_or_want],
      select: %{
        user_id: e.user_id,
        issuer_key: fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer),
        category: e.category,
        need_or_want: e.need_or_want,
        count: count(e.id)
      }
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.group_by(&{&1.user_id, &1.issuer_key})
  end

  defp classify(%{entry: entry, document_id: document_id, issuer_key: issuer_key}, precedents) do
    history = Map.get(precedents, {entry.user_id, issuer_key}, [])
    row = %{entry: entry, document_id: document_id}

    case history |> Enum.map(&completed_booking(entry, &1)) |> Enum.uniq() do
      [] ->
        {:unmatched, Map.put(row, :reason, :no_history)}

      [{category, need_or_want}] ->
        precedent_count = history |> Enum.map(& &1.count) |> Enum.sum()

        {:matched,
         Map.merge(row, %{
           category: category,
           need_or_want: need_or_want,
           precedent_count: precedent_count
         })}

      _conflicting ->
        {:unmatched, Map.put(row, :reason, :conflicting_history)}
    end
  end

  # Precedents only need to agree on what the entry is missing.
  defp completed_booking(entry, precedent) do
    {entry.category || precedent.category, entry.need_or_want || precedent.need_or_want}
  end

  defp apply_matches(_matched, false), do: %{applied: [], failed: []}

  defp apply_matches(matched, true) do
    results = Enum.map(matched, &{&1, apply_match(&1)})

    %{
      applied: for({match, {:ok, _}} <- results, do: match),
      failed:
        for({match, {:error, _step, changeset, _}} <- results) do
          %{match: match, errors: changeset.errors}
        end
    }
  end

  defp apply_match(match) do
    Multi.new()
    |> Multi.update(:entry, booking_changeset(match))
    |> Multi.insert(:event, event_changeset(match))
    |> Repo.transaction()
  end

  defp booking_changeset(%{entry: entry} = match) do
    entry
    |> JournalEntry.changeset_for_categorize(%{
      category: match.category,
      need_or_want: match.need_or_want,
      status: "posted"
    })
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:updated_at, entry.updated_at)
  end

  defp event_changeset(%{entry: entry} = match) do
    EventLog.changeset_for_create(%{
      event_type: @event_type,
      invoice_id: to_string(entry.id),
      user_id: entry.user_id,
      status: "completed",
      metadata: %{
        category: match.category,
        need_or_want: match.need_or_want,
        precedent_count: match.precedent_count,
        previous_status: entry.status,
        previous_category: entry.category,
        previous_need_or_want: entry.need_or_want
      }
    })
  end

  defp format_match(%{entry: entry} = match, verb) do
    "#{verb} entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) as #{match.category} / #{match.need_or_want} " <>
      "from #{match.precedent_count} earlier posting(s)."
  end

  defp format_unmatched(%{entry: entry, document_id: document_id, reason: reason}) do
    "Book by hand: entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) at /documents/#{document_id}: " <>
      unmatched_reason(reason) <> "."
  end

  defp unmatched_reason(:no_history), do: "no earlier posting from this issuer"
  defp unmatched_reason(:conflicting_history), do: "earlier postings disagree"

  defp format_failure(%{match: %{entry: entry}, errors: errors}) do
    "Failed entry #{entry.id}: #{inspect(errors)}"
  end
end

      invoice_id: to_string(entry.id),
      user_id: entry.user_id,
      status: "completed",
      metadata: %{
        category: match.category,
        need_or_want: match.need_or_want,
        precedent_count: match.precedent_count,
        previous_status: entry.status,
        previous_category: entry.category,
        previous_need_or_want: entry.need_or_want
      }
    })
  end

  defp format_match(%{entry: entry} = match, verb) do
    "#{verb} entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) as #{match.category} / #{match.need_or_want} " <>
      "from #{match.precedent_count} earlier posting(s)."
  end

  defp format_unmatched(%{entry: entry, document_id: document_id, reason: reason}) do
    "Book by hand: entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) at /documents/#{document_id}: " <>

  defp unmatched_reason(:conflicting_history), do: "earlier postings disagree"

    "Failed entry #{entry.id}: #{inspect(errors)}"
  end
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfillTest do
  use ZaimuTomo.DataCase, async: true

  import ZaimuTomo.AccountsFixtures, only: [user_fixture: 0, user_scope_fixture: 1]
  import ZaimuTomo.DocumentsFixtures
  import ZaimuTomo.ReviewFixtures, only: [extracted_content_fixture: 3]

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.TaxDeductionClaim

  @event_type "journal_entry_booking_backfilled"

  setup do
    user = user_fixture()
    %{user: user, scope: user_scope_fixture(user)}
  end

  test "a dry run reports the plan and changes nothing", %{scope: scope, user: user} do
    booked(scope, user, "Swisscom", "Utilities", "need")
    entry = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Swisscom")

    assert {:ok, summary} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run()

    assert [%{category: "Utilities", need_or_want: "need", precedent_count: 1}] = summary.matched
    assert summary.applied == []
    assert Repo.reload!(entry).status == "uncategorized"
    assert backfill_events() == []

    report = LegacyBookingBackfill.format_summary(summary)
    assert report =~ "dry run"
    assert report =~ "Would book entry #{entry.id} (Swisscom) as Utilities / need"
  end

  test "confirm books an uncategorized entry from a matching issuer and is repeatable", %{
    scope: scope,
    user: user
  } do
    booked(scope, user, "  SWISSCOM ", "Utilities", "need")
    booked(scope, user, "swisscom", "Utilities", "need")
    entry = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Swisscom", notes: "Keep me")
    last_edit = ~U[2026-03-02 08:00:00Z]
    Repo.update_all(from(je in JournalEntry, where: je.id == ^entry.id), set: [updated_at: last_edit])
    claims_before = Repo.aggregate(TaxDeductionClaim, :count)

    assert {:ok, summary} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)
    assert [%{precedent_count: 2}] = summary.applied

    reloaded = Repo.reload!(entry)
    assert reloaded.category == "Utilities"
    assert reloaded.need_or_want == "need"
    assert reloaded.status == "posted"
    assert reloaded.notes == "Keep me"
    assert reloaded.updated_at == last_edit
    assert Repo.aggregate(TaxDeductionClaim, :count) == claims_before

    assert [event] = backfill_events()
    assert event.invoice_id == to_string(entry.id)
    assert event.user_id == user.id
    assert event.metadata["previous_status"] == "uncategorized"
    assert event.metadata["previous_need_or_want"] == nil

    assert {:ok, again} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)
    assert again.matched == []
    assert length(backfill_events()) == 1
  end

  test "a posted entry keeps its category when precedents only agree on need or want", %{
    scope: scope,
    user: user
  } do
    booked(scope, user, "Mobility", "Transportation", "want")
    booked(scope, user, "Mobility", "Holidays", "want")
    entry = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Mobility")

    Repo.update_all(from(je in JournalEntry, where: je.id == ^entry.id),
      set: [category: "Software", status: "posted"]
    )

    assert {:ok, %{applied: [_]}} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)

    reloaded = Repo.reload!(entry)
    assert reloaded.category == "Software"
    assert reloaded.need_or_want == "want"
  end

  test "leaves entries unchanged without a single agreed precedent", %{scope: scope, user: user} do
    booked(scope, user, "Split", "Transportation", "want")
    booked(scope, user, "Split", "Transportation", "need")
    conflicting = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Split")
    no_history = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Never Seen")

    other = user_fixture()
    booked(user_scope_fixture(other), other, "Other Users Issuer", "Software", "want")
    other_users_issuer = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Other Users Issuer")

    assert {:ok, summary} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)
    assert summary.applied == []

    reasons = Map.new(summary.unmatched, &{&1.entry.id, &1.reason})
    assert reasons[conflicting.id] == :conflicting_history
    assert reasons[no_history.id] == :no_history
    assert reasons[other_users_issuer.id] == :no_history

    assert Repo.reload!(conflicting).status == "uncategorized"

    assert LegacyBookingBackfill.format_summary(summary) =~
             "Book by hand: entry #{no_history.id} (Never Seen) at /documents/"
  end

  defp backfill_events do
    Repo.all(from e in EventLog, where: e.event_type == @event_type)
  end

  defp booked(scope, user, issuer, category, need_or_want) do
    {:ok, entry} =
      scope
      |> legacy_entry(user, issuer)
      |> Accounting.post_entry(user.id, category, need_or_want)

    entry
  end

  defp legacy_entry(scope, user, issuer, opts \\ []) do
    amount = System.unique_integer([:positive])
    document = document_fixture(scope, %{object_key: "documents/legacy-#{amount}.pdf"})

    content =
      extracted_content_fixture(document, user, %{
        extracted_data: %{
          amount_to_pay_cents: amount,
          invoice_date: "2026-03-01",
          invoice_number: nil,
          currency: "CHF",
          reason_for_payment: "Legacy",
          issuer: issuer
        }
      })

    {:ok, _} = Review.create_initial_decision(content)
    {:ok, decision} = Review.approve_invoice(content.id, user.id)
    {:ok, entry} = Accounting.get_journal_entry_for_decision(decision.id)

    Repo.update_all(from(je in JournalEntry, where: je.id == ^entry.id),
      set: [notes: Keyword.get(opts, :notes)]
    )

    Repo.get!(JournalEntry, entry.id)
  end
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfill do
  @moduledoc """
  One-off backfill for journal entries that predate booking at posting time and
  are still missing a category or a need/want choice.

  An entry is completed only when the same user's posted entries from the same
  issuer (compared like the duplicate index, trimmed and case-insensitive) agree
  on every missing value. Values the entry already has are kept. Anything else
  is reported for a person to book, so nothing is guessed from a similar name.

  It is a dry run unless called with `confirm: true`. Each entry is updated in
  its own transaction together with a `journal_entry_booking_backfilled` event
  that records the prior state. Tax claims and notes are left alone, and
  `updated_at` is kept so old entries do not jump to the top of the journal.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias Ecto.Multi
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.EventLog
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision

  @event_type "journal_entry_booking_backfilled"

  @type match :: %{
          entry: JournalEntry.t(),
          document_id: integer(),
          category: String.t(),
          need_or_want: String.t(),
          precedent_count: pos_integer()
        }

  @type unmatched :: %{
          entry: JournalEntry.t(),
          document_id: integer(),
          reason: :no_history | :conflicting_history
        }

  @type summary :: %{
          confirmed: boolean(),
          matched: [match()],
          applied: [match()],
          unmatched: [unmatched()],
          failed: [%{match: match(), errors: term()}]
        }

  @doc """
  Plans the backfill and, with `confirm: true`, applies it.

  Returns `{:error, summary}` only when an update failed. Unmatched entries are
  expected and left for manual booking.
  """
  @spec run(keyword()) :: {:ok, summary()} | {:error, summary()}
  def run(opts \\ []) do
    confirmed = Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false)
    %{matched: matched, unmatched: unmatched} = plan()
    %{applied: applied, failed: failed} = apply_matches(matched, confirmed)

    summary = %{
      confirmed: confirmed,
      matched: matched,
      applied: applied,
      unmatched: unmatched,
      failed: failed
    }

    {if(failed == [], do: :ok, else: :error), summary}
  end

  @spec format_summary(summary()) :: String.t()
  def format_summary(summary) do
    verb = if summary.confirmed, do: "Booked", else: "Would book"
    mode = if summary.confirmed, do: "applied", else: "dry run"

    [
      "Legacy booking backfill (#{mode}): matched=#{length(summary.matched)} " <>
        "applied=#{length(summary.applied)} unmatched=#{length(summary.unmatched)} " <>
        "failed=#{length(summary.failed)}",
      Enum.map(summary.matched, &format_match(&1, verb)),
      Enum.map(summary.unmatched, &format_unmatched/1),
      Enum.map(summary.failed, &format_failure/1),
      if(summary.confirmed, do: [], else: "Nothing changed. Re-run with confirm: true to apply.")
    ]
    |> List.flatten()
    |> Enum.join("\n")
  end

  defp plan do
    precedents = precedents()

    targets()
    |> Enum.map(&classify(&1, precedents))
    |> Enum.group_by(&elem(&1, 0), &elem(&1, 1))
    |> then(&%{matched: Map.get(&1, :matched, []), unmatched: Map.get(&1, :unmatched, [])})
  end

  defp targets do
    Repo.all(
      from e in JournalEntry,
        join: d in ReviewDecision,
        on: d.id == e.review_decision_id,
        join: c in ExtractedContent,
        on: c.id == d.extracted_content_id,
        where: is_nil(e.category) or is_nil(e.need_or_want),
        order_by: e.id,
        select: %{
          entry: e,
          document_id: c.document_id,
          issuer_key: fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer)
        }
    )
  end

  defp precedents do
    from(e in JournalEntry,
      where: e.status == "posted",
      where: not is_nil(e.category) and not is_nil(e.need_or_want),
      where: fragment("btrim(?) <> ''", e.issuer),
      group_by: [e.user_id, fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer), e.category, e.need_or_want],
      select: %{
        user_id: e.user_id,
        issuer_key: fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer),
        category: e.category,
        need_or_want: e.need_or_want,
        count: count(e.id)
      }
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.group_by(&{&1.user_id, &1.issuer_key})
  end

  defp classify(%{entry: entry, document_id: document_id, issuer_key: issuer_key}, precedents) do
    history = Map.get(precedents, {entry.user_id, issuer_key}, [])
    row = %{entry: entry, document_id: document_id}

    case history |> Enum.map(&completed_booking(entry, &1)) |> Enum.uniq() do
      [] ->
        {:unmatched, Map.put(row, :reason, :no_history)}

      [{category, need_or_want}] ->
        precedent_count = history |> Enum.map(& &1.count) |> Enum.sum()

        {:matched,
         Map.merge(row, %{
           category: category,
           need_or_want: need_or_want,
           precedent_count: precedent_count
         })}

      _conflicting ->
        {:unmatched, Map.put(row, :reason, :conflicting_history)}
    end
  end

  # Precedents only need to agree on what the entry is missing.
  defp completed_booking(entry, precedent) do
    {entry.category || precedent.category, entry.need_or_want || precedent.need_or_want}
  end

  defp apply_matches(_matched, false), do: %{applied: [], failed: []}

  defp apply_matches(matched, true) do
    results = Enum.map(matched, &{&1, apply_match(&1)})

    %{
      applied: for({match, {:ok, _}} <- results, do: match),
      failed:
        for({match, {:error, _step, changeset, _}} <- results) do
          %{match: match, errors: changeset.errors}
        end
    }
  end

  defp apply_match(match) do
    Multi.new()
    |> Multi.update(:entry, booking_changeset(match))
    |> Multi.insert(:event, event_changeset(match))
    |> Repo.transaction()
  end

  defp booking_changeset(%{entry: entry} = match) do
    entry
    |> JournalEntry.changeset_for_categorize(%{
      category: match.category,
      need_or_want: match.need_or_want,
      status: "posted"
    })
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:updated_at, entry.updated_at)
  end

  defp event_changeset(%{entry: entry} = match) do
    EventLog.changeset_for_create(%{
      event_type: @event_type,
      invoice_id: to_string(entry.id),
      user_id: entry.user_id,
      status: "completed",
      metadata: %{
        category: match.category,
        need_or_want: match.need_or_want,
        precedent_count: match.precedent_count,
        previous_status: entry.status,
        previous_category: entry.category,
        previous_need_or_want: entry.need_or_want
      }
    })
  end

  defp format_match(%{entry: entry} = match, verb) do
    "#{verb} entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) as #{match.category} / #{match.need_or_want} " <>

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfillTest do
  use ZaimuTomo.DataCase, async: true

  import ZaimuTomo.AccountsFixtures, only: [user_fixture: 0, user_scope_fixture: 1]
  import ZaimuTomo.DocumentsFixtures
  import ZaimuTomo.ReviewFixtures, only: [extracted_content_fixture: 3]

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.TaxDeductionClaim
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.EventLog

  @event_type "journal_entry_booking_backfilled"

  setup do
    user = user_fixture()
    %{user: user, scope: user_scope_fixture(user)}
  end

  test "a dry run reports the plan and changes nothing", %{scope: scope, user: user} do
    booked(scope, user, "Swisscom", "Utilities", "need")
    entry = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Swisscom")

    assert {:ok, summary} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run()

    assert [%{category: "Utilities", need_or_want: "need", precedent_count: 1}] = summary.matched
    assert summary.applied == []
    assert Repo.reload!(entry).status == "uncategorized"
    assert backfill_events() == []

    report = LegacyBookingBackfill.format_summary(summary)
    assert report =~ "dry run"
    assert report =~ "Would book entry #{entry.id} (Swisscom) as Utilities / need"
  end

  test "confirm books an uncategorized entry from a matching issuer and is repeatable", %{
    scope: scope,
    user: user
  } do
    booked(scope, user, "  SWISSCOM ", "Utilities", "need")
    booked(scope, user, "swisscom", "Utilities", "need")
    entry = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Swisscom", notes: "Keep me")
    last_edit = ~U[2026-03-02 08:00:00Z]
    Repo.update_all(from(je in JournalEntry, where: je.id == ^entry.id), set: [updated_at: last_edit])
    claims_before = Repo.aggregate(TaxDeductionClaim, :count)

    assert {:ok, summary} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)
    assert [%{precedent_count: 2}] = summary.applied

    reloaded = Repo.reload!(entry)
    assert reloaded.category == "Utilities"
    assert reloaded.need_or_want == "need"
    assert reloaded.status == "posted"
    assert reloaded.notes == "Keep me"
    assert reloaded.updated_at == last_edit
    assert Repo.aggregate(TaxDeductionClaim, :count) == claims_before

    assert [event] = backfill_events()
    assert event.invoice_id == to_string(entry.id)
    assert event.user_id == user.id
    assert event.metadata["previous_status"] == "uncategorized"
    assert event.metadata["previous_need_or_want"] == nil

    assert {:ok, again} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)
    assert again.matched == []
    assert length(backfill_events()) == 1
  end

  test "a posted entry keeps its category when precedents only agree on need or want", %{
    scope: scope,
    user: user
  } do
    booked(scope, user, "Mobility", "Transportation", "want")
    booked(scope, user, "Mobility", "Holidays", "want")
    entry = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Mobility")

    Repo.update_all(from(je in JournalEntry, where: je.id == ^entry.id),
      set: [category: "Software", status: "posted"]
    )

    assert {:ok, %{applied: [_]}} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)

    reloaded = Repo.reload!(entry)
    assert reloaded.category == "Software"
    assert reloaded.need_or_want == "want"
  end

  test "leaves entries unchanged without a single agreed precedent", %{scope: scope, user: user} do
    booked(scope, user, "Split", "Transportation", "want")
    booked(scope, user, "Split", "Transportation", "need")
    conflicting = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Split")
    no_history = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Never Seen")

    other = user_fixture()
    booked(user_scope_fixture(other), other, "Other Users Issuer", "Software", "want")
    other_users_issuer = legacy_entry(scope, user, "Other Users Issuer")

    assert {:ok, summary} = LegacyBookingBackfill.run(confirm: true)
    assert summary.applied == []

    reasons = Map.new(summary.unmatched, &{&1.entry.id, &1.reason})
    assert reasons[conflicting.id] == :conflicting_history
    assert reasons[no_history.id] == :no_history
    assert reasons[other_users_issuer.id] == :no_history

    assert Repo.reload!(conflicting).status == "uncategorized"

    assert LegacyBookingBackfill.format_summary(summary) =~
             "Book by hand: entry #{no_history.id} (Never Seen) at /documents/"
  end

  defp backfill_events do
    Repo.all(from e in EventLog, where: e.event_type == @event_type)
  end

  defp booked(scope, user, issuer, category, need_or_want) do
    {:ok, entry} =
      scope
      |> legacy_entry(user, issuer)
      |> Accounting.post_entry(user.id, category, need_or_want)

    entry
  end

  defp legacy_entry(scope, user, issuer, opts \\ []) do
    amount = System.unique_integer([:positive])
    document = document_fixture(scope, %{object_key: "documents/legacy-#{amount}.pdf"})

    content =
      extracted_content_fixture(document, user, %{
        extracted_data: %{
          amount_to_pay_cents: amount,
          invoice_date: "2026-03-01",
          invoice_number: nil,
          currency: "CHF",
          reason_for_payment: "Legacy",
          issuer: issuer
        }
      })

    {:ok, _} = Review.create_initial_decision(content)
    {:ok, decision} = Review.approve_invoice(content.id, user.id)
    {:ok, entry} = Accounting.get_journal_entry_for_decision(decision.id)

    Repo.update_all(from(je in JournalEntry, where: je.id == ^entry.id),
      set: [notes: Keyword.get(opts, :notes)]
    )

    Repo.get!(JournalEntry, entry.id)
  end
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Release do
  @moduledoc """
  Release helpers used by deployment tasks.
  """

  @app :zaimu_tomo

  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage.{Migration, Verification}

  def migrate do
    load_app()

    for repo <- repos() do
      {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :up, all: true))
    end
  end

  def rollback(repo, version) do
    load_app()
    {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :down, to: version))
  end

  def migrate_to_s3!(source_dir) when is_binary(source_dir) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Migration.migrate(source_dir), Migration)
  end

  def migrate_to_s3_from_env! do
    System.fetch_env!("SOURCE_DIR")
    |> migrate_to_s3!()
  end

  def backfill_document_fingerprints!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(FingerprintBackfill.run(opts), FingerprintBackfill)
  end

  def verify_storage! do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Verification.verify(), Verification)
  end

  def recover_stuck_documents!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    groups = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.list_stuck()
    Enum.each(groups, &print_stuck_group/1)

    dispatch_recovery(Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false), groups)
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(true, groups) do
    jobs = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.enqueue_stuck(groups)
    IO.puts("Enqueued #{length(jobs)} OCR jobs.")
    groups
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(false, groups) do
    count = groups |> Enum.map(&length(&1.document_ids)) |> Enum.sum()
    IO.puts("Dry run: #{count} stuck documents — nothing enqueued.")
    IO.puts("Re-run with confirm: true (or CONFIRM=true) to enqueue.")
    groups
  end

  defp print_stuck_group(%{user_id: user_id, currency: currency, document_ids: document_ids}) do
    IO.puts("user #{user_id} (#{currency}): document ids #{Enum.join(document_ids, ", ")}")
  end

  defp repos do
    Application.fetch_env!(@app, :ecto_repos)
  end

  defp load_app do
    Application.load(@app)
  end

  defp start_app do
    load_app()

    # Eval nodes run maintenance only: no queues, no plugins, no leadership, so
    # a short-lived node never grabs a job and dies mid-run (leaving it orphaned
    # until Lifeline rescues it).
    oban = Application.fetch_env!(@app, Oban)

    Application.put_env(
      @app,
      Oban,
      Keyword.merge(oban, queues: false, plugins: false, peer: false)
    )

    case Application.ensure_all_started(@app) do
      {:ok, _started} -> :ok
      {:error, reason} -> raise "could not start #{@app}: #{inspect(reason)}"
    end
  end

  defp report_or_raise({status, summary}, formatter) do
    IO.puts(formatter.format_summary(summary))

    case status do
      :ok -> summary
      :error -> raise "storage maintenance command failed"
    end
  end
end

# Operations runbook

Day-2 tasks for the production deployment described in
[deployment.md](deployment.md). Commands assume the Kamal secrets are exported
(`set -a; source .kamal/secrets; set +a`).

## Quick reference

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Remote IEx console | `kamal console` |
| Run migrations | `kamal migrate` |
| Roll back one migration | `kamal db_rollback` |
| App logs | `kamal app logs -f` |
| Find stuck documents (dry run) | `kamal recover_stuck_documents` |
| Re-enqueue stuck documents | `kamal app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.recover_stuck_documents!(confirm: true)'"` |
| Verify every stored object exists | `kamal verify_storage` |
| Backfill document fingerprints | `kamal backfill_document_fingerprints` |

Locally, the equivalents are `mix ecto.migrate`, `mix zaimu_tomo.recover_stuck_documents [--confirm]`, `mix zaimu_tomo.verify_storage`, and `mix zaimu_tomo.backfill_document_fingerprints [--confirm-reuse ID]...`.

## Document processing

### Watching jobs

OCR runs on the Oban `documents` queue and TypeSafe shadow runs on the `typesafe` queue.
There is no Oban Web UI. Inspect jobs from `kamal console`:

```elixir
import Ecto.Query
ZaimuTomo.Repo.all(from j in Oban.Job, where: j.state in ~w(available scheduled executing retryable),
  select: {j.id, j.queue, j.state, j.attempt, j.args})
```

Failed attempts are logged by `ZaimuTomo.ObanFailureLogger` as body-free
summaries. Terminal failures log `[OCR] Processing failed for document …`.
`oban_jobs.errors` holds the same bounded summaries, never OCR text.

### Stuck documents

A document is *stuck* when it has no extraction row and no live OCR job (for
example, a job was discarded or cancelled without recording a failure). Users
can retry stuck and failed documents from the UI. To sweep them in bulk:

1. Dry run: `kamal recover_stuck_documents` lists the stuck documents per user.
2. Enqueue: `kamal app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.recover_stuck_documents!(confirm: true)'"`
   (inside the container, `CONFIRM=true bin/recover_stuck_documents` does the same). This is idempotent, because Oban uniqueness prevents a second live job per document.

### Document fingerprint backfill

Uploads record a SHA-256 of their exact bytes (`documents.content_sha256`), and
postings copy it to `journal_entries.source_document_sha256`. Rows created
before the `20261017120000` migration have no fingerprint until this one-off
backfill reads their objects. The unique index exists before it runs, so it is
safe while the app stays online; no upload or approval pause is needed.

1. Run `kamal backfill_document_fingerprints`. It hashes every document with a
   null digest through the storage facade, then copies digests to journal
   entries one row at a time, oldest posting first. The report lists IDs and
   counts only, never bytes or digests. It exits non-zero while coverage is
   incomplete.
2. Read the report:
   - **Missing object / read failure:** the digest stays null; that document and
     its entries have no exact-file protection. Restore the object if a backup
     has it (then rerun), otherwise record the partial coverage.
   - **Collision:** two historical postings of the same user have identical
     bytes. The later entry stays null and is named with the entry it collides
     with. Nothing is deleted or merged. Review both entries in the ledger:
     a genuine duplicate is corrected through the normal ledger process; a
     legitimate reuse (for example, the same QR-bill for two periods) is
     confirmed by a human.
3. To record a human-confirmed reuse, rerun with the later entry's ID:
   `kamal app exec "bin/backfill_document_fingerprints <journal_entry_id> ..."`
   (locally, `mix zaimu_tomo.backfill_document_fingerprints --confirm-reuse <id>`).
   The entry gets its digest and `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. An
   ID that does not collide is reported as unused and left unchanged.
4. Rerun after any resolution until it reports complete coverage, or until the
   only remaining rows are documented missing objects.

This is the only permitted update of an existing entry's fingerprint. If a
database-level immutability trigger on `journal_entries` is ever added, run the
backfill first or allow this update explicitly.

### Throttling

If the LLM provider rate-limits, set a lower `OBAN_DOCUMENTS_CONCURRENCY` (default 2)
or `TYPESAFE_MAX_CONCURRENCY` under `env.clear` in `config/deploy.yml` and redeploy. Locally, set
`OBAN_DOCUMENTS_CONCURRENCY=1` with a single-NPU FastFlowLM backend.

## Backups and restore

Data lives in two places that must be backed up **together and in order**:
RustFS objects first, then the PostgreSQL dump. Objects are created before rows
are inserted, and rows are deleted before objects. So an object export that is
older than the DB dump can contain only harmless orphan objects, never missing
ones.

Nightly, while document writes are quiet:

1. Export the bucket through the S3 API with `rclone copy --checksum --immutable` to a **new date-stamped path** on off-host storage, then `rclone check --checksum`. Use an rclone S3 remote with `provider = Other` and `force_path_style = true`, a read-only credential, and the RustFS region. Don't snapshot RustFS's `/data` directory while it is live.
2. `pg_dump` the production database to off-host storage.
3. Run `kamal verify_storage`.

Restore (also used for periodic restore drills on a scratch environment):
restore the object export first, then the Postgres dump, then run `bin/verify_storage`.
It must report zero missing and zero failed.

Backup credentials and destinations are not kept in the repository.

## Legacy upload volume

Before August 2026, document bytes lived in `priv/uploads` on a Docker volume
(`zaimu_tomo_uploads`). The migration release copied them to RustFS with
`bin/migrate_to_s3` (HEAD first, upload only missing objects, never overwrite or
delete) and verified them with `bin/verify_storage`. The volume mount in
`config/deploy.yml` and the directory in the `Dockerfile` remain until a restore
check is recorded. After that, remove both in a cleanup release and update
[architecture.md §11](architecture.md#11-risks-and-technical-debt).

## Database access

The Postgres accessory's host port listens only on loopback. Use an SSH tunnel
from the operator machine, or `kamal accessory exec db "psql -U zaimu_tomo zaimu_tomo_prod"`.

# Operations runbook

Day-2 tasks for the production deployment described in
[deployment.md](deployment.md). Commands assume the Kamal secrets are exported
(`set -a; source .kamal/secrets; set +a`).

## Quick reference

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Remote IEx console | `kamal console` |
| Run migrations | `kamal migrate` |
| Roll back one migration | `kamal db_rollback` |
| App logs | `kamal app logs -f` |
| Find stuck documents (dry run) | `kamal recover_stuck_documents` |
| Re-enqueue stuck documents | `kamal app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.recover_stuck_documents!(confirm: true)'"` |
| Verify every stored object exists | `kamal verify_storage` |
| Backfill document fingerprints | `kamal backfill_document_fingerprints` |
| Complete legacy bookings (dry run) | `kamal app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.backfill_legacy_bookings!()'"` |
| Complete legacy bookings (apply) | `kamal app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.backfill_legacy_bookings!(confirm: true)'"` |

Locally, the equivalents are `mix ecto.migrate`, `mix zaimu_tomo.recover_stuck_documents [--confirm]`, `mix zaimu_tomo.verify_storage`, and `mix zaimu_tomo.backfill_document_fingerprints [--confirm-reuse ID]...`.

## Document processing

### Watching jobs

OCR runs on the Oban `documents` queue and TypeSafe shadow runs on the `typesafe` queue.
There is no Oban Web UI. Inspect jobs from `kamal console`:

```elixir
import Ecto.Query
ZaimuTomo.Repo.all(from j in Oban.Job, where: j.state in ~w(available scheduled executing retryable),
  select: {j.id, j.queue, j.state, j.attempt, j.args})
```

Failed attempts are logged by `ZaimuTomo.ObanFailureLogger` as body-free
summaries. Terminal failures log `[OCR] Processing failed for document …`.
`oban_jobs.errors` holds the same bounded summaries, never OCR text.

### Stuck documents

A document is *stuck* when it has no extraction row and no live OCR job (for
example, a job was discarded or cancelled without recording a failure). Users
can retry stuck and failed documents from the UI. To sweep them in bulk:

1. Dry run: `kamal recover_stuck_documents` lists the stuck documents per user.
2. Enqueue: `kamal app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.recover_stuck_documents!(confirm: true)'"`
   (inside the container, `CONFIRM=true bin/recover_stuck_documents` does the same). This is idempotent, because Oban uniqueness prevents a second live job per document.

### Document fingerprint backfill

Uploads record a SHA-256 of their exact bytes (`documents.content_sha256`), and
postings copy it to `journal_entries.source_document_sha256`. Rows created
before the `20261017120000` migration have no fingerprint until this one-off
backfill reads their objects. The unique index exists before it runs, so it is
safe while the app stays online; no upload or approval pause is needed.

1. Run `kamal backfill_document_fingerprints`. It hashes every document with a
   null digest through the storage facade, then copies digests to journal
   entries one row at a time, oldest posting first. The report lists IDs and
   counts only, never bytes or digests. It exits non-zero while coverage is
   incomplete.
2. Read the report:
   - **Missing object / read failure:** the digest stays null; that document and
     its entries have no exact-file protection. Restore the object if a backup
     has it (then rerun), otherwise record the partial coverage.
   - **Collision:** two historical postings of the same user have identical
     bytes. The later entry stays null and is named with the entry it collides
     with. Nothing is deleted or merged. Review both entries in the ledger:
     a genuine duplicate is corrected through the normal ledger process; a
     legitimate reuse (for example, the same QR-bill for two periods) is
     confirmed by a human.
3. To record a human-confirmed reuse, rerun with the later entry's ID:
   `kamal app exec "bin/backfill_document_fingerprints <journal_entry_id> ..."`
   (locally, `mix zaimu_tomo.backfill_document_fingerprints --confirm-reuse <id>`).
   The entry gets its digest and `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. An
   ID that does not collide is reported as unused and left unchanged.
4. Rerun after any resolution until it reports complete coverage, or until the
   only remaining rows are documented missing objects.

This is the only permitted update of an existing entry's fingerprint. If a
database-level immutability trigger on `journal_entries` is ever added, run the
backfill first or allow this update explicitly.

### Throttling

If the LLM provider rate-limits, set a lower `OBAN_DOCUMENTS_CONCURRENCY` (default 2)
or `TYPESAFE_MAX_CONCURRENCY` under `env.clear` in `config/deploy.yml` and redeploy. Locally, set
`OBAN_DOCUMENTS_CONCURRENCY=1` with a single-NPU FastFlowLM backend.

## Backups and restore

Data lives in two places that must be backed up **together and in order**:
RustFS objects first, then the PostgreSQL dump. Objects are created before rows
are inserted, and rows are deleted before objects. So an object export that is
older than the DB dump can contain only harmless orphan objects, never missing
ones.

Nightly, while document writes are quiet:

1. Export the bucket through the S3 API with `rclone copy --checksum --immutable` to a **new date-stamped path** on off-host storage, then `rclone check --checksum`. Use an rclone S3 remote with `provider = Other` and `force_path_style = true`, a read-only credential, and the RustFS region. Don't snapshot RustFS's `/data` directory while it is live.
2. `pg_dump` the production database to off-host storage.
3. Run `kamal verify_storage`.

Restore (also used for periodic restore drills on a scratch environment):
restore the object export first, then the Postgres dump, then run `bin/verify_storage`.
It must report zero missing and zero failed.

Backup credentials and destinations are not kept in the repository.

## Legacy upload volume

Before August 2026, document bytes lived in `priv/uploads` on a Docker volume
(`zaimu_tomo_uploads`). The migration release copied them to RustFS with
`bin/migrate_to_s3` (HEAD first, upload only missing objects, never overwrite or
delete) and verified them with `bin/verify_storage`. The volume mount in
`config/deploy.yml` and the directory in the `Dockerfile` remain until a restore
check is recorded. After that, remove both in a cleanup release and update
[architecture.md §11](architecture.md#11-risks-and-technical-debt).

## Database access

The Postgres accessory's host port listens only on loopback. Use an SSH tunnel
from the operator machine, or `kamal accessory exec db "psql -U zaimu_tomo zaimu_tomo_prod"`.
